native.admission_inspect: Stiff linen, hemmed in seven short stitches. Plain, if you do not linger.
apply_texts: A second reading moves the long stitch one place left. The card was not turned.
On this last press the stitches lie still. The wrong gap does not widen.
Pressed flat, a faint resin scent. Seven stitches. One sits a hair higher.
The count slips as you press. Six, then a gap. Your hand is steady. The thread is not.
The gaps suggest a phrase, then withdraw it. Naming them does not make them agree.
The hem repeats. You can leave the count wrong. The linen allows it.
The pattern answers the looking: one stitch more, where your thumb already was.
You count back from the end. Eight stitches, or the first was a crease-shadow.
You count seven. The seventh stitch shortens under your thumb. You did not pull it.
You set the card down mid-count. The unease thins by a degree, no more.
You stop counting. The hem goes almost even. The relief is small and unexplained.
inspect_texts: A thumb-creased linen card. Seven stitches hem the edge. Resin in the cloth.
Each look moves a stitch. You are not sure the moving is in the thread.
From the other end the hem shows eight. The extra may be a crease-shadow.
Only linen and thread. The count will not stay where you leave it.
Seven stitches, spaced like rests in a tune not sounded. Only linen.
Stiff linen, hemmed in seven short stitches. Plain, if you do not linger.
The fourth gap is wider than the third. It was not, a moment ago.
The gaps are a pattern now, or you made them one. The card will not say.
The hem will not hold a count. Six, then seven, then a gap.
The hem will not match itself. Each count ends on a different stitch.
The stitches crawl if you hold the count. Look away: only thread again.
You counted seven. The seventh stitch is shorter now, as if the thread crept.
native.name: Hemmed Pitch-Card
